ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (amended 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data and Transaction Records Preservation (PBOC Order No. 1 [2007], as amended); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Commercial Franchise (2007).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate foreign investor (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies House / corporate registry of the investor's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention state: notarize the certificate, obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority, then obtain a certified Chinese translation. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille state: notarize the certificate, authenticate it through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then obtain consular legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state, followed by a certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry / registrar of companies in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel rule: notarization plus Apostille if the issuer is an Apostille member; or notarization plus foreign-ministry authentication plus Chinese consular legalization if the issuer is a non-member; then certified Chinese translation. Never combine both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign investor approving WFOE incorporation and granting power of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / duly authorized corporate secretary, with notarization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the board resolution, then apply an Apostille if the issuer's country is an Apostille member; otherwise obtain foreign-ministry authentication and Chinese consular legalization. Add a certified Chinese translation. The two authentication paths are alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / constitutional documents of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or company secretary, as certified copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate the certified copy by notarization plus Apostille (member state) or notarization plus foreign-ministry authentication plus Chinese consular legalization (non-member state), then provide a certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank (relationship manager signature and bank seal, notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter on bank letterhead, notarized, then either Apostille by the competent authority if the bank's country is an Apostille member, or foreign-ministry authentication plus Chinese consular legalization if the bank's country is a non-member; append a certified Chinese translation. Do not chain apostille with consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before bank account opening and at every ownership change, screen all direct and indirect shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories and any person holding proxy against: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list; UN Security Council Consolidated List; EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists (where parent group has EU/UK nexus); Chinese domestic sanctions and anti-money laundering blacklists; PBOC terrorist financing list; Ministry of Commerce export control/catch-all lists; and judicial execution/tax non-payment list. A minimum 25% UBO threshold applies, but lower thresholds and control-based identification are required for PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions. Enhanced due diligence must include source-of-funds evidence, corporate documentary chain, and negative news corroboration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must have a registered Chinese-language company name. An English name may be recorded only as a supplementary foreign name and is not a substitute. The name must follow the four-tier composite order: administrative division or trade prominence, distinctive mark, industry and operational characteristics, and

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (comprehensively revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 5, 23-32, 42-51, 53, 60-65; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4-6 and 28-29; Regulations on the Registration Management of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746, 2022), Articles 2, 8-14 and 26; Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) 2024 Edition; Regulation on the Administration of Commercial Franchises (State Council Order No. 485, 2007).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal or District Market Supervision Administration in whose jurisdiction the WFOE registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and the Articles of Association submitted through the SAMR integrated online market entity registration system, followed by issuance of the Business License with Unified Social Credit Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to this WFOE under the PRC Company Law or Foreign Investment Law. The registered capital amount and contribution schedule are set in the Articles of Association; under the 2023 Company Law, subscribed capital must be fully paid within five years from incorporation unless a shorter sectoral rule applies. There is no blocked escrow account requirement. The capital must be wired to a dedicated capital contribution account at a licensed bank in China, and use of the capital must comply with the Articles, foreign exchange control rules, and anti-money-laundering requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (WFOE). I, the undersigned, being all of the Directors of [Company Name] Limited (the Company), lawfully acting as the first Board of Directors of the Company in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Company's Articles of Association, do hereby adopt the following resolutions by unanimous written consent in lieu of the first board meeting, effective immediately. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. RESOLVED that the registered capital of the Company is fixed at [RMB _______], divided into [_______] equal capital contribution units of RMB 1.00 each, and that the capital subscription schedule set forth in the register of contributions is approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Directors shall procure that each shareholder pays the subscribed contribution in full into the Company's dedicated capital contribution account promptly and in any event within the statutory five-year contribution period; that the Board accepts such contributions; that the Company issues a capital contribution certificate to the shareholder; and that the Legal Representative is authorized to execute any capital verification, filing, or proof-of-payment documents required by Chinese law. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the Company shall establish its principal banking relationship with a commercial bank licensed in the People's Republic of China. The Chairman, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized to open the basic deposit account, a capital contribution account, a foreign currency savings account, and any ancillary settlement accounts; to enroll as authorized signatories; to apply for online banking, POS merchant settlement, and wire transfer facilities; and to execute account mandates, loan and collection documents, bank confidentiality waivers, and any forms required to receive franchise royalty remittances from overseas and domestic franchisees through wires or local POS payments. All banking forms and account designation resolutions are approved and ratified. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is adopted as [full registered address], People's Republic of China. The Legal Representative and General Manager are directed to execute and deliver the lease or proof-of-use right certificate, to file that address with the local Market Supervision Administration, to maintain statutory registers at the registered office, and to display the Company name plaque and statutory business license in compliance with Chinese law. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED that the following persons are appointed as the Company's statutory officers: [Name] as Chairman and Legal Representative; [Name] as General Manager; [Name] as Supervisor; [Name] as Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] as Company Secretary or administrative manager. Each appointment shall take effect upon this Resolution and shall continue until a subsequent board resolution or the General Meeting removes or replaces the officer. The Legal Representative is specifically authorized to sign all registration filings, tax filings, labor contracts, lease contracts, food safety applications, franchise disclosure documents, and other regulatory documents in connection with the formation and operation of the Company. The Supervisor is instructed to supervise the Board and management, to review the capital contribution and bank account records, and to verify that all statutory filings are timely made. 5. IMPLEMENTATION AND RATIFICATION. RESOLVED that all preliminary acts, contracts, engagements, payments, registrations, Powers of Attorney, notarizations, legalizations, lease arrangements, and applications made in good faith before the date of this Resolution on behalf of the Company are hereby authorized, ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects. RESOLVED FURTHER that this Resolution is effective immediately and shall bind the Company, its shareholder, directors, officers, agents, and successors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Negative List screening and company name pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR office) through the provincial integrated online government service portal; National Development and Reform Commission and Ministry of Commerce negative-list consultation portal if needed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal review against the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) to confirm that bubble tea restaurant operations and franchise administration are in the permitted category; if a prohibited or restricted item appears in the proposed scope, delete it before filing. Prepare and submit an online application for pre-approval of the WFOE name with at least three alternative names in the format jurisdiction plus brand element plus industry plus corporate nature. Verify that the selected name does not conflict with an existing enterprise, trademark, or protected name. Attach the foreign investor's certificate of good standing and identity documentation, notarized, apostilled or legalized and translated into English/Chinese as required, and submit the proposed Articles of Association to the local Market Supervision Administration platform. The result is the Name Pre-Approval Notice, which will be used in the next step.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Pre-approval of Enterprise Name
Proposed Articles of Association (draft)
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of the foreign shareholder, notarized and apostilled/legalized
Power of attorney to the application agent if any
Negative List compliance statement
Proposed registered address proof or letter of intent for lease
Identity documents of proposed legal representative, directors, supervisor and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is queried because of duplication or similarity, promptly select one of the alternative names and resubmit through the same portal. If the negative-list compliance statement is questioned, amend the business scope to exclude restricted items and provide an explanatory cover letter. The applicant should cure any query or suspension within five working days to preserve the application queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation registration and issuance of the Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) market entity registration window or the provincial integrated online registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Name Pre-Approval Notice, submit the full establishment application, the signed Articles of Association, the proof of registered office use, and the identity documents of the statutory officers to the local Market Supervision Administration. The filing must state the exact WFOE name, registered address, business scope, total registered capital, contribution schedule, legal representative, directors, supervisor, and general manager. For foreign shareholders, attach the legalized and translated corporate documents; ensure all signatures and seals comply with Chinese notarization requirements. Electronically sign the application or physically present original documents at the registration window. The regulator will review the submission for name compliance, capital legality, negative-list conformity, address validity, and officer eligibility, then issue the Business License bearing a Unified Social Credit Code. The WFOE acquires legal person status on the date of issue.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application
Articles of Association executed by all shareholders
Name Pre-Approval Notice
Proof of right to use the registered office (lease contract or property certificate)
Identity/passport copies of legal representative, directors, supervisor and general manager
Notarized and apostilled/legalized foreign investor documents
Statement confirming no sector requiring state approval
Authorized representative notice where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authority issues a rectification notice, correct all deficiencies and resubmit within the specified statutory period, generally fifteen working days. If a business scope description is rejected, narrow it to the approved services and food operations. If an officer appears disqualified, replace that person by shareholder written decision and amend the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company seal engraving, bank account opening, and paid-in capital injection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-designated seal engraving service; licensed commercial bank under the People's Bank of China; Safe Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Business License, arrange for engraving of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal at a Public Security Bureau-approved engraving shop; file the seal specimens with the local Public Security Bureau. Open the Basic Deposit Account at a licensed commercial bank in the city of registration, together with a working capital account and a dedicated capital contribution account for the subscribed registered capital. Complete the bank's KYC and AML questionnaire by providing the corporate ownership chart, source of funds, beneficial owner information, business relationship profile, and expected payment rails, including franchise royalty wire transfers and local POS settlements. Deliver the Board Resolution on banking authorization and signatory mandates to the bank. After the foreign shareholder remits the capital contribution, convert or receive the funds in the capital contribution account and obtain the capital contribution payment receipt and bank-issued foreign exchange report.
required_dossiers: Original WFOE Business License
Company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and seal-record certificate
Bank account authorization resolution and board resolution
Passport/ID of legal representative and finance officer
Power of attorney for bank account openers
Rent contract, utility invoice and site proof for bank KYC
AML forms, UBO declaration and source-of-funds statement
Capital contribution schedule and foreign wire instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide a detailed corporate chart, certified copy of the shareholder's passport and business registration, and proof that the registered capital is sourced from legal business operations. If the foreign exchange receipt is queried, work with the bank to correct the SWIFT details and re-file the foreign currency receipt report within fifteen days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, payroll setup, social insurance, and housing fund activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; local Housing Fund Management Center.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the Business License data has automatically completed tax registration through the multi-license data-sharing mechanism; if not, file the supplemental tax registration at the local tax service hall. Update the taxpayer profile with the legal representative, finance officer, bank account and registered address. Register employees in the social insurance system for pension, medical, work-injury, unemployment and maternity insurance, and in the housing fund system; sign labor contracts with each employee within one month of employment. Activate the payroll system and the official invoice management system. Apply for VAT general taxpayer status if projected annual revenue exceeds the relevant regulatory threshold, and connect the in-store POS systems to the tax invoice API so that franchise store sales and local receipts can be reported. Establish the corporate income tax quarterly prepayment and annual reconciliation calendar.
required_dossiers: Business License copy
Tax registration information if not automatically integrated
Articles of Association and bank account confirmation
Taxpayer identification and payroll authorization letter
Employment contracts and employee registration list
Identification of principal financial officer and tax representative
Lease records and registered office documents for tax locality
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late filing or penalty notices appear, respond immediately with a voluntary correction statement and request administrative leniency under the Tax Collection Administration Law. If social insurance registration is rejected due to employee document gaps, cure the identity and contract deficiencies and resubmit within ten working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food business licensing, environmental registration, and fire safety clearance for bubble tea premises and syrup support facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (food business and food production licensing); Municipal Ecological Environment Bureau; local Fire and Rescue Department under the Ministry of Emergency Management.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before opening any bubble tea store, franchise demonstration store, warehouse, or central syrup formulation facility, submit a food license application to the local Market Supervision Administration and request an on-site inspection of the premises. For ordinary beverage and food sales at each store, obtain the Food Business License covering catering service. If the WFOE manufactures, blends, bottles or re-packs syrups at any central facility, obtain the Food Production License for that facility. In parallel, evaluate the project against the EIA classification list and submit an environmental registration/filing form to the Municipal Ecological Environment Bureau if required; no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is expected for small-scale catering but must be confirmed if the syrup facility uses process equipment, boilers, or discharges industrial wastewater. Submit premises floor plans, fire safety designs, and emergency evacuation plans to the Fire and Rescue Department and obtain the Fire Safety Inspection Certificate before opening the premises to the public.
required_dossiers: WFOE Business License
Lease or property rights certificate for each premise
Site plan and kitchen/storage layout
Food safety management system and sanitation policy
Food business or food production license application form
Legal representative identity and food safety manager appointment certificate
Employee health certificates
Water quality report if applicable
Grease trap and waste disposal agreements
Fire safety design documents and evacuation plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the food authority reports an inspection deficiency, complete the required rectification and request a follow-up inspection within the statutory window. If the fire certificate is withheld, remedy exit width, fire extinguisher, signage, alarm, or occupancy-load deficiencies and resubmit. If the EIA filing is questioned, submit a site-specific pollution prevention statement or a revised classification memorandum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial franchise filing, franchise disclosure, and foreign exchange royalty collection procedure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce provincial commerce department or local commercial bureau; SAFE and the designated settlement bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the WFOE will act as franchisor in China, register the first franchise agreement with the competent commercial department within fifteen days after the first franchise contract is signed and maintain a complete copy-ready franchise disclosure document and franchise operation manual in English and Chinese as applicable. Verify and document the franchisor maturity requirements, including direct-store operating history or an exemption memorandum based on the foreign master franchisor model. Open the payment structure for franchise royalties through bank wire or local POS, and where international royalties are received, file the relevant foreign exchange record with the bank under SAFE current-account rules. Maintain annual filing updates and franchisee termination notices, and keep records of all franchise agreements, disclosures, fees, and operational support materials for at least five years.
required_dossiers: Commercial Franchise Filing Report
First franchise agreement sample
Franchise Disclosure Document
Franchise Operations Manual
Evidence of direct-operated stores or franchisor qualification memorandum
WFOE Business License and legal representative identity documents
Board resolution appointing franchise filing officer
Bank account confirmation and foreign exchange instruction sample
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial department challenges the two-store-one-year requirement or completeness of the disclosure package, provide the foreign franchisor's audited financial statements, operating records, and lawful exemption analysis. If the franchise filing is rejected, correct the documents and refile, or file an administrative reconsideration within sixty days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Market Supervision Administration for food licenses; Municipal Ecological Environment Bureau for EIA registration and pollution control; local Fire and Rescue Department under the Ministry of Emergency Management for fire safety; Ministry of Commerce provincial commercial authority for commercial franchise filing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business License (Catering Service) for each bubble tea store and franchise demonstration store; Food Production License for any central syrup blending, bottling, or food processing facility; Commercial Franchise Filing and Franchise Disclosure Document for the franchise licensing program; Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for each public gathering venue.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE), acting through the local Municipal Ecological Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category coding under the EIA Classification List for Construction Projects (2021): small bubble tea shops and a franchise office are generally at the environmental registration/filing or exempt tier. A full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required unless a central syrup production facility with food processing wastewater, boilers, solvent cleaning, or substantial energy combustion is established. If the WFOE engages only in franchise licensing and advisory services with no physical kitchen or production at its head office, the EIA can be stated as Not Applicable at the head office; each store or processing facility must be separately evaluated and registered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All commercial kitchen and beverage-preparation wastewater must pass through grease traps and sand traps before discharge to the municipal sewer. Unless a stricter local standard applies, the applicable limits under the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard (GB 8978-1996) are chemical oxygen demand less than or equal to 500 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand less than or equal to 300 mg/L, suspended solids less than or equal to 400 mg/L, animal and vegetable oils less than or equal to 100 mg/L, and pH between 6 and 9. Kitchen oil fumes shall be treated using fume purification equipment with filtration efficiency equal to or greater than 85 percent, and exhaust stacks shall be installed so that no black smoke or offensive odor reaches neighboring properties. Volatile organic compound emissions from any solvent or cleaning operation, if present, must comply with the national comprehensive VOC treatment plan and local emission control limits. Waste cooking oil, spent food oil, and food sludge must be transferred to a licensed recycler under a signed manifest; hazardous waste such as chemical cleaners or solvent waste, if generated, must be stored in labeled containers and removed by an entity holding the appropriate hazardous waste permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The WFOE and each food-serving or public-access premises must obtain the Public Gathering Premises Fire Safety Inspection Certificate before opening. The local Fire and Rescue Department must verify fire lanes, emergency exits, fire extinguishers, automatic fire alarm and sprinkler coverage, smoke exhaust measures, and evacuation signage. Engineering clearance must include structural load inspection of any mezzanine seating, kitchen equipment platforms, cold rooms, and syrup storage racks. Occupational safety approval requires a workplace safety policy, designated safety manager, emergency plan, first-aid supplies, documented employee training, and for all food handlers, valid health certificates. The food safety manager must hold a recognized PRC food safety management certificate, and any central facility handling or storing modest quantities of cleaning solvents must obtain the applicable fire-danger operation permit from the local fire rescue authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating the National Electronic Tax Administration Portal (e-Tax) and the provincial e-Tax platforms for digital filing, VAT invoice validation, and tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For this WFOE structure, the entity is a Chinese resident limited liability company. Upon issuance of the business license by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) 18-digit identifier is automatically generated and serves as the enterprise Tax Identification Number (TIN). Within 30 days of business license issuance, the WFOE must complete supplementary tax registration through the National Electronic Tax Administration Portal (e-Tax), selecting the competent tax authority, confirming general VAT taxpayer status or small-scale taxpayer status, and applying for VAT invoice quota and tax control authorisation. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a WFOE, the same portal allocates a separate Non-Resident Enterprise TIN through the withholding agent upon filing of the contract and relevant documentation under the STA's Notice on Non-Resident Tax Payer Identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (China does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election for entity classification; all resident enterprises including WFOEs are taxed at entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Provisional Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value-Added Tax, administered jointly with the State Taxation Administration's Golden Tax Phase IV system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for basic tax registration - mandatory upon business license issuance. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; below this threshold, small-scale taxpayer status applies with a 3% (or reduced 1%) levy rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: General VAT taxpayers must use the State Taxation Administration's national electronic invoice service platform to issue Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices (FDEI) and special VAT invoices. Every invoice is transmitted in real-time to the STA's Golden Tax Phase IV system, carries a unique electronic tax control number and QR authentication code, and is cleared against the central tax database before the buyer can legally use it for input VAT credit. Business systems must integrate with the e-Tax portal via STA-certified fiscal API interfaces; no paper or offline invoice is permitted for B2B transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods physically leaving China through customs declaration are eligible for 0% VAT and full refund of input VAT, provided the exporter has general taxpayer status and the goods are officially recorded on an export customs declaration. Qualifying cross-border services (including franchise licensing and overseas royalties supplied to a foreign franchisee) are eligible for zero-rating or exemption where the service recipient is an overseas enterprise, the services are rendered and consumed entirely outside China, and the taxpayer has filed the cross-border taxable service exemption/zero-rating filing with the competent tax authority before claiming the treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration Form (Customs Bill of Entry for Export)
Original Bill of Lading (ocean/air/road) with onward shipment evidence
Commercial invoice and export sales contract
Bank receipt confirming inward foreign exchange for the export consignment (Export Proceeds Collection Slip with FX settlement record)
Foreign exchange payment/remittance certificate issued by a licensed bank in China for the export proceeds
Export VAT invoice (FDEI or special VAT invoice) endorsed with zero rate
Cross-border Taxable Service Exemption/Zero-Rating Filing (Filing Certificate) where service components are included
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law and the Measures for the Administration of Export Tax Rebates, any export zero-rating claim that fails audit or is proved fraudulent triggers retrospective clawback of all VAT refunded (including input credits), imposition of a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and administrative fine from 50% to 500% of the falsely obtained refund. If the false export scheme is determined by the tax authority or customs to constitute fraudulent export tax rebate, criminal liability under the Criminal Law applies, with penalties ranging from fixed-term imprisonment to life imprisonment in aggravated cases, plus confiscation of property. The STA and General Administration of Customs jointly conduct random cross-verification of export declaration data, shipping records, and FX repatriation within the 180-day window and may extend audits retroactively to all previously zero-rated transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), under the policy direction of the People's Bank of China (PBOC), is the central regulator for all foreign exchange, cross-border settlement, and capital account flows within mainland China.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is conditionally convertible on current account items and tightly controlled on capital account items. Since 1996, China maintains current account convertibility, so royalty payments, trade settlement, service charges, and interest can move cross-border once genuine trade receipts are verified by the bank and SAFE. All current account payments require an underlying contract/invoice and are subject to post-event verification. Capital account items, including FDI equity injections, domestic loans from offshore lenders, dividends, and liquidation proceeds repatriation, require SAFE registration, approval, or filing, and are not freely convertible. Foreign shareholders' capital must enter through a designated FDI capital escrow/foreign exchange settlement account, be verified by the receiving bank, and only be converted into RMB against actual business expenses. Profit remittance by a WFOE is permissible via current account channels after annual financial audit, final tax settlement, and issuance of tax payment certificates; dividends are also subject to withholding tax and SAFE remittance filing. Export receipts are not subject to mandatory conversion but must be repatriated onshore and recorded in SAFE's monitoring system. Overall, convertibility is genuine but only through licensed banks, with purpose codes and documentary audit trails enforced.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to China within 180 days from the customs export declaration date, unless an extension is granted by the bank or SAFE in specific circumstances. The current statutory mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent for ordinary current account trade receipts, because China abolished blanket surrender requirements; however, all receipts must be credited to a domestic foreign exchange settlement account held by the WFOE, and any conversion into RMB must be backed by the export invoice, customs declaration, logistics documents, and the SAFE trade item matching system. Retained foreign currency may be used for eligible current-account payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low / not legally viable for primary treasury use. Mainland China does not recognise foreign fintech EMIs as licensed payment institutions or deposit-taking banks under the PBOC Administrative Measures for Online Payment. Such EMI platforms cannot open domestic RMB settlement accounts, cannot clear CNY through CNAPS/CIPS, and cannot act as the receiving bank for FDI capital injection or outbound forex remittances. They may be used only as ancillary customer-facing technology rails when partnered with a licensed Chinese bank, and must comply with data localisation and cybersecurity assessment rules. The WFOE's treasury must therefore rely on tier-1 domestic banks; any purported EMI corporate account should be rejected in AML underwriting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE corporate account opening, the legal representative or a board-appointed signatory holding a notarised power of attorney must normally appear physically at a Chinese bank branch for an in-person KYC interview. Remote opening is not generally available for initial foreign-invested entity accounts. Consular legalisation of the POA is accepted, but the authorised agent still has to present original identification documents at the branch. Banks may permit video teleconference for follow-up compliance reviews, not for the first risk-based onboarding interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and control-chain opacity caused by offshore holding companies or nominee shareholders interposed above the WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete corporate ownership diagram showing each entity and natural person above the WFOE; certificates of incorporation and registry extracts for every intermediate entity; notarised copy of passports for all natural persons owning 25% or more; signed UBO declaration; board resolution appointing the legal representative; and bank references from the investor's home country bank verifying the source of the investment funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent source of wealth and source of funds for the registered capital, especially when funds are routed through multiple jurisdictions or into third-party trust/omnibus accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit six months of pre-transfer bank statements from the remitting shareholder, a certified source-of-wealth report covering accumulated savings, employment income tax records, business profit and dividend records, sale contracts or property transfer deeds for asset disposals, and the signed capital contribution commitment letter; include certified translations where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags in syrup/tea ingredient import-export flows where invoice prices deviate significantly from benchmark commodity values or payment beneficiaries differ from logistics parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain the full transactional trail: purchase orders, commercial contracts with Incoterms, original commercial invoices, full sets of bills of lading/airway bills, packing lists, customs export declarations, insurance certificates, and SAFE trade item matching reports; add an independent valuation report from a certified commodity/industry expert if the price is non-standard, plus intra-group transfer pricing documentation if the supplier is affiliated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty outflows to an offshore brand/trademark licensing entity that may be a disguised profit repatriation or royalty stripping arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide trademark and IP registration certificates, the franchise license agreement approved by the relevant Chinese authorities, MOFCOM/SAFE registration proof, withholding tax payment vouchers and tax clearance certificate, executed Form FDI/current-account remittance applications, and an arm's-length royalty valuation prepared by a licensed tax or transfer pricing advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The FDI capital injection must be remitted from the shareholder's overseas bank account via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 message to the WFOE's dedicated capital escrow account (FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account) held with a SAFE-qualified bank. The remittance should use the purpose code 'FDI Equity Injection' or the corresponding Chinese direct investment code approved by SAFE, and must reference the WFOE's FDI registration certificate. After receipt, the WFOE files the actual receipt under SAFE's management system, obtains a bank-issued foreign investment capital verification letter, and completes required investment information reporting to the local Commerce Bureau. For a limited liability company structured in 2024, paid-in capital must be injected within the time limit set by China's Company Law and the articles, generally no more than five years. The bank will monitor the use of the capital account funds and require payment against actual business transactions before converting the escrowed foreign currency into RMB for operating expenditure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import of franchise equipment, tea leaves, syrups, and branded packaging, the WFOE can use SWIFT MT103 for low-value service fees, royalties, and ordinary trade payments under an invoice or contract; Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight or usance) are recommended for large capital equipment imports; Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are suitable for established supplier relationships. Every outbound current account payment must be executed via a licensed bank with genuine trade documentation, including contract, invoice, customs declaration, and transport/tax records where applicable. Outbound royalties to a foreign franchisor require a registered licensing agreement, tax withholding, and SAFE remittance application; direct capital account outward payments require separate approval and are not routed through routine trade clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY forward contracts with licensed banks under the real demand principle, covering only projected trade or royalty exposures documented by underlying contracts.
FX swaps combining spot and forward transactions for converting USD/HKD capital into RMB and reversing upon genuine dividend or trade transactions.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the overseas parent entity as a hedge of offshore RMB exposure, because the onshore WFOE cannot access speculative NDF markets.
Cross-currency swaps restricted to hedging the currency mismatch of an actual offshore loan facility of the WFOE, with the notional amount not exceeding the loan principal and interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Report (Annual Report) under the Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year, covering the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days after the deadline; if unrectified for 3 consecutive years, placement on the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List with joint disciplinary sanctions, administrative fines up to RMB 100,000, restriction of legal representatives, and potential administrative revocation of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Final Settlement (Annual Reconciliation) Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By May 31 each year for the prior calendar year (within 5 months of fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax; compulsory tax enforcement, blocked invoice issuance, restriction on credit ratings, and potential criminal liability for tax evasion if fraudulent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) - Foreign Investment Information Reporting System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year for the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Written corrective order; failure to rectify within the prescribed period attracts a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 500,000 (serious cases); repeated violations may trigger cross-department disciplinary actions and impact foreign exchange, customs, and banking facilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: WFOEs are unconditionally subject to annual statutory audit by a PRC-licensed CPA firm irrespective of revenue, total assets, headcount, or balance sheet size. The mandate arises from the Law on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises and its Implementing Rules. For other Chinese companies, statutory audit is compulsory for: (i) listed public companies; (ii) financial institutions (banking, insurance, securities, funds); (iii) state-owned enterprises and state-controlled mixed-ownership companies; (iv) companies designated by SAMR or the Ministry of Finance for targeted supervision; and (v) entities applying for special administrative licensing or public bidding where audited financial statements are required by law. No general national quantitative thresholds (turnover/assets/headcount) exempt a WFOE from the mandatory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS, converged with IFRS); small-scale enterprises may apply the Accounting Standards for Small Business Enterprises (ASSBE) if eligible under MOF criteria, but WFOEs typically apply full CAS. Fiscal year is the calendar year (January 1 to December 31).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the SAMR/PBOC Beneficial Ownership Information Measures (effective November 1, 2024), the WFOE must file beneficial ownership particulars with SAMR within 30 days of incorporation or any change in beneficial ownership, including transfers of shares or changes in ultimate controlling interests. In each annual enterprise report filed via NECIPS between January 1 and June 30, the WFOE must confirm shareholder and control-chain information, which serves as the annual UBO confirmation. There is no separate annual UBO return absent a triggering change, but the 30-day post-change reporting window remains mandatory.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors, Supervisors and Senior Management
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 for a simple small WFOE; USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 for a mid-sized franchise/supply-chain entity with cross-border royalty flows and inventory

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises with taxable income up to RMB 3 million pay an effective 5% until the end of 2027; High and New Technology Enterprises pay 15%; qualifying R&D expenditures are allowed a 100% additional deduction; no general statutory tax holiday applies to a boba tea franchise or syrup supply WFOE in mainland China. Free trade zone 15% preferential rates are limited to encouraged industries and do not normally apply here.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (A Class) Form A100000 and supplementary schedules; filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system (e-Tax / Electronic Tax Bureau portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly advance filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly advance EIT returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end; the annual final return, financial statements, and related-party transaction reporting schedules are due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (by 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue (Main Business Revenue plus Other Business Revenue).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross franchise royalties, initial franchise fees, boba tea syrup sales, equipment sales, and onsite training fees earned by the WFOE. Foreign currency receipts are translated into RMB at the spot exchange rate at the date of payment or PBOC benchmark rate for the period. Cross-border amounts must be traceable to conclusive commercial contracts. Do not net out cost of sales. If revenue relates to exports of syrups to overseas franchisees, customs export declarations and bank receipt records should reconcile to the declared amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating costs (cost of goods sold and direct service costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include costs of tea leaves, milk, fruit, packaging, and direct labor related to production of syrups. Purchases from affiliated foreign suppliers must be arm's length and supported by customs declarations, import invoices, and transfer pricing documentation. Non-resident related-party costs without substance or a benefitting party will be subject to tax adjustment.

Declare urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp tax, property tax, and land use tax. Corporate income tax and VAT are not deducted here. Outbound service VAT paid on royalties is not a deductible corporate income tax item unless capitalised according to applicable rules.

Intercompany management fees, brand licensing royalties paid abroad, and global headquarter cost allocations are deductible only when evidenced by a service agreement, benefitting party analysis, actual services, and arm's-length fees. If the WFOE pays a non-resident parent a royalty or management fee, it must perform withholding tax obligations before deducting the expense; otherwise the deduction is denied.

Add back penalties, excessive entertainment expenses, unqualified invoices, and non-arm's-length related-party expenditures. Subtract tax-exempt income and allowable additional deductions, including a 100% additional deduction for R&D expenses incurred for beverage formula and supply chain technology development. Cross-border losses or intangible migration transactions require special adjustment analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after prior-period losses set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply tax losses carried forward within five years; taxable income cannot be reduced by transactions lacking economic substance. This is the line where transfer pricing adjustments and general anti-avoidance rule add-backs are reflected. The line is computed on a resident entity basis; non-resident shareholders do not file their dividend and royalty income on this form; those amounts are taxed through withholding procedures at distribution or payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise income tax payable at applicable statutory or preferential rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 25% headline rate unless the WFOE validly qualifies for the small low-profit enterprise effective 5% rate or the high-tech enterprise 15% rate. Deduct quarterly advance tax prepayments and foreign tax credits for income already taxed abroad. Distributed profits must not contain unpaid CIT; the net amount after this line becomes the base for the 10% dividend withholding tax when declared to a non-resident parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, pre-payments, and net enterprise income tax payable in final settlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the annual tax liability with quarterly advances. If the WFOE is the withholding agent for outbound dividend, interest, or royalty income, it files separate withholding tax returns; the annual corporate return does not include the non-resident tax payable. Failure to withhold the 10% WHT from foreign-parent dividends exposes the WFOE to joint and several liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return under TCAL Article 62 risks a penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 if a previous tax inspection found late filing; late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue amount under TCAL Article 32. Material false reporting is tax evasion under TCAL Article 63 and may be criminally prosecuted under Criminal Law Article 201 when the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax payable; deliberate concealment with false invoices may additionally trigger tax blacklisting and travel bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% under Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 37 and 38 (final withholding on dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident recipient).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner of the dividends and submit a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty state's tax authority, together with the Chinese treaty relief application form, to the withholding agent before distribution. The WFOE as withholding agent must file the application and supporting documents with the competent Chinese tax authority, including the shareholding structure, shareholding period, and evidence that the parent is not a pass-through or conduit company. Only when the reduced treaty rate is substantiated may it be applied; otherwise 10% WHT must be withheld and the excess may be reclaimed through the annual reconciliation or refund process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident WHT is 10% on gross royalty and interest income from PRC sources, plus 6% VAT on royalties when the licensor is a non-resident enterprise under VAT rules. Under applicable bilateral double tax treaties, interest and royalty rates are generally reduced to 10%, and some treaties provide a 5% royalty withholding rate or interest exemptions for financial institutions; the relevant treaty must be applied through the same beneficial-owner and Tax Residency Certificate procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where controlled transactions in a tax year involve tangible asset transfers over RMB 200 million, or intangible asset transfers, financial asset transfers, loans, or services over RMB 100 million; Master File is required when aggregate controlled transaction value in any fiscal year exceeds RMB 1 billion. A WFOE must also file the Annual Related Party Transaction Report together with the annual EIT return regardless of these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply offshore-type economic substance regulations to ordinary WFOEs, but Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and the substance-over-form doctrine empower tax authorities to disregard artificial arrangements. The WFOE must perform its core income-generating activities, including franchise contract negotiation, quality control, syrup formulation, procurement, logistics, franchisee marketing, and management of related-party risks. If these CIGAs are conducted outside China or by the foreign parent while all profits are booked in the WFOE, the tax authority may recharacterize the entity as a conduit, deny treaty benefits, and assess tax on the real beneficiary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Round-Tripping Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Chinese WFOE with no employees, no real business premises, no local management, and no active performance of franchise support or syrup supply functions, solely to book taxable profits in China and then route dividends to a foreign parent without any real economic operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 is the general anti-avoidance rule authorizing special tax adjustments and denial of tax benefits; additional CIT plus a 0.05% daily late-payment surcharge may be assessed. Administrative blacklisting under the joint punishment memorandum on tax collection restricts the entity's financing, tax clearance, and exit from China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If directors sign false annual financial statements or cause the shell company to deny obligations, courts may pierce the corporate veil under PRC Company Law Article 23 and impose personal liability for company debts and unpaid taxes. Directors can also be placed on the individual tax blacklist, receive travel bans, and be disqualified from serving as senior managers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Base Erosion via Intercompany Charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive royalties, management fees, and technical service fees to a non-resident parent; imports raw materials at inflated prices; and under-charges foreign franchisees for syrup exports, all without contemporaneous Local File documentation or arm's-length pricing substantiation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41-44, the tax authority may recharacterize intercompany payments, deem excessive royalties as non-deductible distributions, and impose interest on underpaid tax. If the conduct amounts to tax evasion, TCAL Article 63 permits recovery of the underpaid tax plus a fine of 0.5 to 5 times the tax amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executives who intentionally create false related-party records may not hide behind the corporate entity; PRC Company Law Article 23 allows personal asset restitution for misappropriation, and Criminal Law Article 201 can subject controlling officers to imprisonment of up to seven years with personal fines for willful tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion, Money Laundering, and False Accounting of Franchise Cash Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing POS sales, requiring franchisees to pay cash outside the books, fabricating purchase invoices, using personal bank cards of directors to collect franchise fees, and making undisclosed offshore payments through shell accounts to avoid Chinese corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Article 201 and TCAL Article 63 impose liability for unpaid tax and fines ranging from 50% to 500% of the evaded amount; criminal penalties can range from up to three years' imprisonment for minor evasion to up to seven years for substantial evasion where the amount exceeds 30% of tax payable and is above RMB 100,000. The Anti-Money Laundering Law may additionally impose penalties up to RMB 5 million for non-compliant payment transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for tax debts where they personally received or controlled suppressed cash flows; civil restitution can attach to personal assets; the director will be blacklisted by tax authorities and subjected to travel restrictions; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment up to seven years plus confiscation of property used in money laundering.
